description: Large-scale Ridesharing DARP Instances Based on Real Travel Demand is a data set deposited in IEEE DataPort by its authors David Fiedler (Czech Technical University in Prague). This dataset presents a set of large-scale Dial-a-Ride Problem (DARP) instances. The instances were created as a standardized set of ridesharing DARP problems for the purpose of benchmarking and comparing different solution methods.The instances are based on real demand and realistic travel time data from 3 different US cities: Chicago, New York City, and Washington ... Coverage: not stated; the metadata date the deposit to 2023. The formats are not stated in the metadata. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge, and IEEE DataPort normally asks for a free account before download (not tested). The licence is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related record: the repository-level record data-ieeedp-repository.
